Subject: [Urgent] p95/p99 spikes, 502s over last 40m

Hi Monica —

We started seeing a sharp rise in p95 and p99 latency for the hosted inference endpoint (model: redwood/fast-13b) around 07:30 EDT. Between 07:30 and 07:50 we had periodic 502s and timeouts; overall throughput dropped ~30% while error rate climbed to ~1.8%. Attaching a quick screenshot and a tiny list of trace ids.

This is impacting our fraud-detection scoring pipeline (batch window is slipping) — we have a daily SLA and will miss internal SLAs if this persists. Can your team confirm whether this is a model or infra issue? The traces look like long queuing before execution.

Thanks Aisha / Monica —

Quick summary of what I’m seeing from infra: around 07:28–07:42 we experienced a brief surge in incoming QPS from a small set of customers; the serving runtime’s batching service increased queue depth to maintain throughput which in turn pushed tail latencies up. A few requests hit internal timeout thresholds and returned 502.

Preliminary hypotheses:
- Aggressive batching/backpressure interaction: the continuous-batching loop increased batch size to chase throughput, but when downstream kernel scheduling lagged (CUDA kernel queueing), per-request waiting time spiked.
- KV cache misses on longer sequences amplified per-token execution time for those requests, pushing more requests into the queue.

Immediate asks for FinSolve: can you share a few full request payloads (or sanitized summaries) for the trace ids you attached? Also confirm whether FinSolve switched any client-side retry/backoff configs in the last 24 hours. Those details will help confirm if it's customer traffic pattern or internal kernel scheduling.

What we’re doing now:
- Rolling a temporary change to the batching policy for the affected pool to cap max batch size and reduce queue depth.
- Enabling additional tracing for kernel scheduling and per-request wait time.

I’ll post updates after the change completes (~09:20).

— Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

A few requests hit internal timeout thresholds and returned 502.

Thanks Sean. We checked — the traffic pattern for FinSolve was steady during that window (no client-side spikes) and we did not change retries. The traces attached include full sanitized payloads for the three request-ids you mentioned. We also found that our scheduler retried three requests after a 1s backoff, which may have contributed to queueing.

This is high impact: 2 downstream scoring jobs missed the SLA and triggered alerts in our ops during morning batch run. Our CTO is asking for an exec-level note and a mitigation timeline. Please include whether Redwood will adjust routing/backoff suggestions or if FinSolve should change client retries to avoid backpressure amplification.

Aisha

Marissa —

Forwarding an escalation from FinSolve (external). TL;DR: their p95/p99 jumped for hosted-api in us-east-1 between 07:28–07:42; we believe batching + queue depth increase during a short kernel-scheduling stall caused elevated tail latency and several 502s. FinSolve confirmed they did not spike client traffic but did have three retried requests that could have contributed.

Immediate mitigation we implemented: capped max batch size for the affected serving pool and turned on per-kernel scheduling tracing. Early telemetry shows a drop in p95 (from ~1.4s to ~0.7s) for the window after the change, and 502s have fallen back to baseline. We still need to:

- Confirm root cause with the kernel traces (Sean) and determine whether a permanent batching policy change or a kernel backoff is required.
- Produce a short customer-facing post-mortem for FinSolve within 48 hours explaining cause, mitigation, and recommended client backoff guidance.

Customer ask: FinSolve wants an explicit recommendation on client retry/backoff best practices to avoid amplifying queue depth; they are also asking whether Redwood can provide temporary increased concurrency for the next scheduled batch window tomorrow (their daily run).

Related links: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.prod/d/ops/requests?from=now-1h&to=now | HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/FinSolve

Can you prioritize the kernel-trace analysis and confirm whether we should: (a) make the batch cap change permanent for that pool, (b) schedule a controlled change to the kernel scheduler, or (c) coordinate with Finance to provide a temporary concurrency bump for FinSolve tomorrow?

I’ll coordinate the customer post-mortem draft once we have root-cause language.

— Monica
